w14.002: Appendix XXIV, The Third Experiential Trinity (pp. 485–494)
w14.003: Sadler treats the second level of the Trinity of Trinities as a genuine trinity in its own right, which he names the third experiential Trinity. Its three members are the Supreme, the Ultimate, and the Limited-Absolute; the last is the deity presence of God the Absolute as He will appear through trinitization. If the Paradise Trinity was the first of all trinities, this one is the last. It can be formed, but it can never be fully unified, because infinity cannot be used up.
w14.004: 1. The First Trinity and the Last (orig. pp. 485–486)
w14.005: Whenever Sadler turns his mind to the far future, he likes to hold up the far past as a mirror. Looking closely at absolute causes, he believes, gives a dim outline of what events near absolute destiny may be like. In this appendix he uses the same approach once more, this time to examine the Trinity of Trinities and above all its second level.
w14.006: Long ago, in past eternity, the Universal Father joined the Eternal Son to trinitize the Infinite Spirit and to eternalize the central universe. With the appearance of the third person the existential cycle of Deity personalization was complete, and among the three there arose the decisive interdependence of which The Urantia Book speaks.
w14.008: Sadler expects a pattern of the same shape to recur in the remote future. Building on a finished master universe, God the Supreme and God the Ultimate would together trinitize God the Absolute and open the inner zone of the Cosmos Infinite. A cycle of experiential Deity personalization would then begin, and a trinitarian interdependence would arise once again, this time among three experiential Deities.
w14.009: The two events resemble each other, yet they move in opposite directions. The first moves from the Father alone to Father and Son and then to all three, Father, Son, and Spirit; Sadler calls it “intensifying,” a deepening inward. The second runs from the Supreme, to Supreme and Ultimate, and on to an Absolute held within limits; this one he calls “extensifying,” a widening outward. There is also one basic difference. The Son originates from the Father, whereas the Ultimate does not originate directly from the Supreme.
w14.010: Two Deity trinitizations: the first, in the eternal past, and the future one that Sadler envisions
w14.011: 2. The Trinity of Trinities: Its Second Level (orig. pp. 486–487)
w14.012: According to The Urantia Book, the Trinity of Trinities has a first level made up of three trinities (Paradise, Ultimate, and Absolute), while the second level is the union of the three experiential Deity personalities [106:8.20]. Sadler identifies the occupant of the third seat on that second level as the deity presence of God the Absolute, appearing by trinitization. When the three experiential Deities come together, a new system emerges, and in that emergence he sees the third experiential Trinity being factually formed. He rests the idea on a question the revelation itself asks.
w14.014: In an earlier appendix (XIX) Sadler proposed that every experiential trinity passes through three stages: qualified reality, factual formation, and unified reality. Laid over the second level, the scheme reads as follows. This level has been a qualified reality since the opening of the second universe age, as Majeston, actualized on that level, bears witness. Once God the Absolute has been trinitized, it can be factually formed at any time. Yet it never reaches the third stage of unification, because the Limited-Absolute cannot exhaust infinity.
w14.015: Like the Other Trinities, Yet Unlike Them
w14.016: Sadler insists that no two trinities are alike. The third experiential Trinity resembles the Paradise Trinity because it is formed through a Deity trinitization, and it resembles the Trinity Absolute because it can never be wholly unified. It differs from every other trinity, however, in being the only one that sits inside a larger trinity, an internal trinity.
w14.017: 3. Members of the Final Trinity (orig. pp. 488–490)
w14.018: Sadler counts three members: Supreme Deity functioning as coabsolute (or coinfinite), Ultimate Deity of the same status, and the deity presence of the Limited-Absolute trinitized by the Supreme-Ultimate. Naming the third member is awkward. “God the Absolute” suggests a person, while the Deity Absolute is a purely existential potential. He therefore sets this member apart from the Absolute that knows no limits and calls it the Limited-Absolute.
w14.019: The Urantia Book names three superfinite possibilities for the manifestation of the Supreme Being in the universe. The third is this:
w14.021: From this third possibility Sadler reasons that the Supreme Being keeps growing even after His personality is complete. The growth is not beyond personality; it is growth that comes after power-personalization has been finished. He applies the same reasoning to Ultimate Deity. Both experiential Deities take part in projecting experience onto a field of creative expression outside the master universe, and the revelation calls those who share in that work coabsolutes [106:0.7].
w14.022: The third member is more complicated. Sadler sees this presence moving through three phases. At first it is an initial presence, no larger than what the Supreme-Ultimate has trinitized. Next it becomes an increasing presence, growing by an eternal power-personality synthesis. Finally, if every process could be completed, it would be a hypothetical final presence that experientially binds the three Absolutes into one. Since the infinite potential of the three Absolutes is never used up, however, that third phase never arrives.
w14.023: 4. Functions of the Final Trinity (orig. pp. 490–491)
w14.024: Forming a trinity does not erase its members. The Father and the Son, though they have become as one, keep their own identities, and the Paradise Trinity does not hide the individuality of the three persons or their accessibility. What changes is the manner of Deity function.
w14.026: Sadler expects the same in the future. God the Supreme, God the Ultimate, and God the Absolute could each be contacted as individuals, but in relation to the total universe they would act only as a trinity. He also suspects that, just as Havona was a universe of Trinity origin that appeared together with the first Trinity, the inner zone of the Cosmos Infinite may be a universe that appears together with the last. This trinity grows without end and keeps moving toward unity, yet it is never finished. Precisely because it stays unfinished, the adventure of the universe and its citizens never meets a final wall.
w14.027: Approaching the Universal Absolute Versus Reaching It
w14.028: The revelation describes the Universal Absolute as open to experiential-existential approach [0:11.14]. Sadler points out that approaching is not the same as arriving. Since the incomprehensibility of the Universal Absolute deepens as the universe expands [10:8.8], the expansion may outrun the approach. (The original cites this passage as 0:1.14.)
w14.029: 5. The Last Attempt at Experiential Deity Unification (orig. pp. 491–494)
w14.031: Existential Deity is eternally one in the Paradise Trinity. The unity of experiential Deity, by contrast, depends on the efforts of every creator, Deity, and trinity after Havona. Sadler arranges these efforts as a sequence of attempts on three levels.
w14.032: Three levels of experiential Deity unification (Sadler's arrangement)
w14.034: Emerges when the level's activity ends
w14.035: Master universe, second to sixth ages
Emerges when activity ends; Trinity Absolute cannot be unified
w14.036: God the Absolute; third experiential Trinity
Emerges when activity begins; never completed
w14.037: The first two levels are what the revelation calls “⟦Q 0:12.1⟧two subabsolute and evolutional levels⟦/Q⟧” [0:12.1]. On these levels a Deity and a trinity emerge when the work of the level is done. The third level, by contrast, is no subabsolute level at all but the original absolute one from which the other two were projected, and here the order is reversed. Because neither infinity nor eternity can be exhausted, there is no moment when the work is finished, so the new Deity and the new trinity appear when the work begins. Sadler finds a likeness here to the opening of the first universe age, when Deity likewise personalized as the age began rather than as it closed.
w14.038: The three members of the second level can thus be described as evolutionary-experiential Deity (the Supreme), transcendental-experiential Deity (the Ultimate), and existential-experiential Deity (the Limited-Absolute). Sadler reads this unifying but never unified trinity as a final effort to gather together, by experiential means, what the Infinite once divided by existential means in eternity. What the effort aims at, he adds, is not a new Deity but the original Deity: an experiential attempt to enter into the Infinite.
w14.039: The Trinity of Trinities and the "internal trinity" within it (the reading of the second level is Sadler's inference)
w14.040: Sadler regards the second level of the Trinity of Trinities as a true trinity: the third experiential Trinity, or Final Trinity.
w14.041: Its three members are the Supreme, the Ultimate, and the Limited-Absolute; the last is the deity presence of God the Absolute once He has been trinitized.
w14.042: The Father-Son trinitization intensifies Deity inward; the Supreme-Ultimate trinitization extends Deity outward.
w14.043: This trinity can be formed but never unified, since quantitative infinity can never be exhausted.
w14.044: Within the trinity each member keeps its individuality; only Deity function toward the total universe is joined as a trinity.
w14.045: Experiential Deity unification is attempted on finite, subabsolute, and absolute levels, and on the third level the Deity and the trinity appear at the beginning of the activity.
w14.046: God the Absolute in His Trinitized Nature
w14.047: Appendix XXV, The Trinitized Nature of God the Absolute (pp. 495–500)
w14.048: Sadler expects the trinitization of God the Absolute to be the greatest outburst of creative power since the personalization of the Infinite Spirit. This appendix sketches the nature of God the Absolute as He will then appear. He is the Limited-Absolute: not infinite, yet undiminished in quality. In nature He resembles the Son; in trinity relationship He resembles the Infinite Spirit. He grows forever, both as person and as Deity, yet never reaches infinity. Through that growth a way opens to know the Father-as-Absolute by experience.
w14.049: 1. The Trinitization of the Absolute (orig. pp. 495–496)
w14.050: When the Infinite Spirit appeared, the eternal central universe came into being and the first universe age began. Sadler believes the appearance of God the Absolute will be an event of comparable weight: the start of a peripheral universe reaching into infinity, and the opening of the last universe age.
w14.051: In the eternal past the Father and the Son trinitized without any limitation, and the result was an infinite being equal to both. The Supreme and the Ultimate, however, are not infinite. The revelation calls them derived Deities.
w14.053: That does not make them lesser Gods. Together they are almighty Deities who have gathered into themselves, by power-personality synthesis, the whole finite and absonite potential of the master universe. Sadler reasons that what their trinitization produces, though not infinite, will not be diminished in quality. The limit lies in quantity, not in quality, and this is what the name Limited-Absolute is meant to convey.
w14.054: He goes a step further. The revelation says that the Third Source and Center is more than the sum of the Father and the Son.
w14.056: If so, God the Absolute may likewise appear as greater than the Supreme and the Ultimate added together, greater even than the Supreme-Ultimate. Still, the two events are alike without sharing the same structure. In Sadler's words the later one is less a parallel of the first than a mirror image of it. The Father and the Son sought to break out of infinity; the Supreme and the Ultimate seek to break into it.
w14.057: 2. The Nature of God the Absolute (orig. pp. 496–498)
w14.058: By origin, God the Absolute stands to the Supreme-Ultimate much as the Infinite Spirit stands to the Father-Son. The Son is an unqualified existential-absolute person; God the Absolute is an experiential-absolute person in a qualified sense. Sadler sums it up this way: in nature He is like the Son, and in trinity relationship He is like the Infinite Spirit. Insofar as He is existential, He resembles both; insofar as He is experiential, He resembles neither.
w14.059: One distinction is easy to miss. The God the Absolute of the Foreword is the completed, unlimited experiential unification of the three Absolutes. The God the Absolute whom Sadler is now considering is a subinfinite version of that unification. If He is nevertheless undiminished in quality, the revelation's portrait of God the Absolute offers a guide to His nature. Sadler identifies four features.
w14.060: Four characteristics of God the Absolute as Sadler describes Him
w14.062: God the Supreme is personal and God the Ultimate is superpersonal; God the Absolute is Deity beyond superpersonality.
w14.063: Since the Ultimate already functions on the final creative level, any function beyond it is post-creative or supercreative.
w14.064: If completed, absolute meanings would be unified, but the unification of absolute values remains an open question.
w14.065: It runs from personal through superpersonal to the border of the impersonal; beyond it lies the Unqualified Absolute.
w14.066: On the third point Sadler adopts the revelation's own careful reservation.
w14.068: All of this concerns realities very far from present experience. Sadler nevertheless believes that this exploration will one day become our own task, because finaliters carry the gifts of personality and the Adjuster, which make growth beyond the ultimate possible.
w14.070: 3. How the Limited-Absolute Grows as a Person (orig. pp. 498–499)
w14.071: God the Absolute, appearing through trinitization, is undiluted absolute in nature but still incomplete absolute in universal function. He is an experiential actualization of existential potential, yet at the moment of His appearing He has not yet functioned experientially; He has never personally taken part in power-personality synthesis. His growth begins afterward.
w14.072: Sadler first considers the comparatively simpler matter of personal growth. (Strictly speaking, he notes, the right term would be transcended superpersonality, but he says “personal” for convenience.) Whatever part of the Deity Absolute's potential the Supreme-Ultimate trinitization did not reach remains outside God the Absolute. He grows by gradually taking that outer potential into Himself. As the Paradise Trinity activates the Deity Absolute existentially [10:8.4], God the Absolute within the second-level trinity will activate it experientially, though only to a limited degree. This growth has no end.
w14.073: 4. How the Limited-Absolute Grows as Deity (orig. pp. 499–500)
w14.074: Growth as Deity is harder to picture, because it involves all three Absolutes. The emergence of the Supreme Being completes power-personality synthesis on the finite level, and the emergence of the Ultimate completes it on the transcendental level. Sadler expects the same kind of synthesis to continue on the absolute level, where it would amount to an attempt to bind the three Absolutes experientially into one.
w14.075: That goal, however, is beyond the reach of the Trinity Absolute, of the third experiential Trinity, and even of the Trinity of Trinities. The revelation says so plainly.
w14.077: Sadler reads this not as a dead end but as the dynamic of growth that never stops. Seen from the far reaches of the Cosmos Infinite, where God the Absolute will venture with the Supreme and the Ultimate, the entire master universe may shrink to a nuclear creation, and natives of the Quartan Space Level may be classed with Havoners as folk of the “inner universes.” And because the reality of God the Absolute is experiential, He opens a way to know the Father-as-Absolute by experience, qualitatively though never quantitatively. It is a knowing always bounded yet always widening. Were the bounds to vanish, the growth would stop as well.
w14.078: Sadler sees the trinitization of God the Absolute as the greatest creative event since the personalization of the Infinite Spirit and as the dawn of the final universe age.
w14.079: The Supreme and the Ultimate are derived Deities, so the result of their trinitization is not infinite; yet the limit is one of quantity, not quality. Hence the name Limited-Absolute.
w14.080: In nature God the Absolute resembles the Son; in trinity relationship He resembles the Infinite Spirit.
w14.081: Sadler describes His nature under four heads: transcended superpersonality, supercreative function, unity of meanings and values, and final Deity expression.
w14.082: God the Absolute grows forever, both personally and as Deity, yet never encompasses the three Absolutes entirely.
w14.083: That growth opens a way to know the Father-as-Absolute qualitatively, by experience.
w14.085: Appendix XXVI, Functions of the Supreme-Ultimate (pp. 501–507)
w14.086: Sadler regards the Supreme-Ultimate as a functional bridge between the master universe, the nucleus, and the Cosmos Infinite, its cytoplasm. The Supreme-Ultimate is not a single person. It is a Dual-Deity partnership to be formed in the far future, a level of function that already exists, and the outer limit of experiential reality. What the revelation says about the Supreme-Ultimate Mind, the Solitary Messengers, and the Trinitized Sons of Destiny serves as evidence that this future function is already being prepared.
w14.088: The Urantia Book often lists these three side by side: Supreme, Ultimate, Supreme-Ultimate [13:1.18]. Sadler understands the last name to be of the same kind as “Father-Son”: a name for the union of a Dual-Deity that comes into being through the adventure of trinitization.
w14.089: When the Father joined with the Son, He limited Himself in one respect only.
w14.091: Sadler expects the Supreme-Ultimate to be similar. In certain phases the two act inseparably together, but elsewhere each of the two Deities can be reached, and each acts, on His own. He summarizes the Supreme-Ultimate in three ways. First, together with the Father-Son, it is one of only two Dual-Deity partnerships that begin with a Deity trinitization. Second, although the partnership itself belongs to the distant future, a Supreme-Ultimate level of function has existed since the dawn of time. Third, it marks the farthest limit to which experiential reality can extend toward the absolute; beyond it the experiential joins with the existential.
w14.093: The revelation never speaks of a “Son-Spirit mind,” yet it does speak of a Supreme-Ultimate Mind. Sadler weaves an intriguing set of clues around this.
w14.095: The Solitary Messengers were all created at once, and they are very old. The Supreme-Ultimate Mind, then, was bestowed at the dawn of time. Yet the Supreme-Ultimate partnership will not be formed until after the sixth age. In whose keeping does that mind rest in the meantime? Sadler looks for an analogy in the mind of the Supreme. While the Supreme Being is evolving, the potential of that mind is held by the Seven Master Spirits [116:1.3]. The Master Spirits, moreover, hold as a group the supreme-ultimate attributes of the Third Source and Center.
w14.097: Sadler therefore infers that the Seven Master Spirits may hold in trust not just the mind of the Supreme but the mind of the Ultimate and the Supreme-Ultimate Mind as well.
w14.098: The clues go further. The Master Spirits are also the ones who sanction the mixed unions in which a finaliter and a Paradise-Havona citizen trinitize together, and the Trinitized Sons of Destiny born of those unions are linked with the Supreme-Ultimate Mind.
w14.100: Each of these sons is assigned a Solitary Messenger, and the two remain as a pair in the secret college of the Creator Son corps on Vicegerington. Solitary Messengers connected with the origin of the Supreme-Ultimate Mind; Sons of Destiny produced by a repercussion in that mind; and the fact that the pair should dwell precisely on the world of the Creator Sons: Sadler judges this to be more than coincidence. He sees it as preparation for the post-ultimate ages, when the Creator Sons will hold a changed status and the still unrevealed work of the Supreme-Ultimate will at last be actualized.
w14.101: Clues surrounding the Supreme-Ultimate Mind (dashed links are Sadler's inferences)
w14.102: 3. Function in the Master Universe (orig. pp. 504–506)
w14.103: The revelation states that the personal presences of the Supreme and the Ultimate are already found in Havona [14:6.29]. Of the Supreme-Ultimate, however, it speaks as “⟦Q 13:2.10⟧the future Supreme-Ultimate⟦/Q⟧” [13:2.10]. As a partnership its function is still pure potential. Even so, the Supreme-Ultimate as a level of function is operating now.
w14.105: From this passage and the section that follows, Sadler draws three conclusions. The Supreme-Ultimate level borders on the absolute and contains the whole of the absonite. This level now operates within the union of the Seven Master Spirits. Its scope, however, ends with the master universe and does not reach into the Cosmos Infinite. In addition, the classification of Havona's activities even includes an item called “⟦Q 14:6.4⟧Supreme-Ultimate evolutional⟦/Q⟧” [14:6.4]. Sadler takes this as evidence that the central universe has already foreseen, and provided for, the future activity of the Supreme-Ultimate.
w14.106: 4. Function in the Cosmos Infinite (orig. pp. 506–507)
w14.107: If the master universe is viewed as a universe standing alone, the Supreme-Ultimate level is the ceiling of growth. But the revelation speaks of a level at which experiential reality is projected onto a wider field beyond the master universe, and it calls that level coabsolute [106:0.7]. Among the seven classes of Havona life, the sixth is in fact coabsolute and the seventh absolute [14:4.7].
w14.108: Sadler expects the Supreme-Ultimate to be formed after the sixth universe age closes and to become the first Dual-Deity active in the Cosmos Infinite. Just as the Father-Son took the lead in making the first universe, the central creation, the Supreme-Ultimate will be the first to link the nuclear master universe with the cytoplasmic Cosmos Infinite. The revelation, however, mentions a name lying even farther out.
w14.110: Beyond the Supreme-Ultimate stands the Ultimate-Absolute. Sadler wonders whether it may be another Dual-Deity, one that will arise in the far reaches of the Cosmos Infinite, and he carries the question forward to the next appendix.
w14.111: Sadler regards the Supreme-Ultimate as a functional bridge linking the nuclear master universe and the cytoplasmic Cosmos Infinite.
w14.112: The Supreme-Ultimate is not a person but a Dual-Deity partnership; it is also a level of function that exists now and the limit of experiential reality.
w14.113: Like the Father-Son, the Supreme-Ultimate acts as one only in certain phases; elsewhere the two Deities act individually.
w14.114: The Seven Master Spirits collectively hold the supreme-ultimate attributes, and Sadler infers that they are the interim custodians of the Supreme-Ultimate Mind.
w14.115: The Solitary Messengers, the Trinitized Sons of Destiny, and the secret college on Vicegerington are clues to preparation for the post-ultimate ages.
w14.116: The Supreme-Ultimate will be the first Dual-Deity active in the Cosmos Infinite, and beyond it lies the Ultimate-Absolute.
w14.117: The Growth of the Cosmos Infinite
w14.118: Appendix XXVII, Growth of the Cosmos Infinite (pp. 508–519)
w14.119: In his final appendix Sadler tests how far concepts can carry us into the Cosmos Infinite. The trinitization of God the Absolute, he suggests, will bring a “beachhead on the shores of infinity” suddenly into being: the inner zone of the Cosmos Infinite. He divides the Cosmos Infinite into inner, intermediate, and outer zones and pairs them with three post-universe ages and three Dual-Deities. He also rebuilds the seven levels of Total Deity function as existential-experiential levels.
w14.120: 1. Echoes of the Supreme-Ultimate Trinitization (orig. pp. 508–509)
w14.121: The Supreme and the Ultimate express the entire finite and absonite potential of the master universe, and as the Supreme-Ultimate they sum it up. Sadler sees their trinitization of God the Absolute as the projection of that sum beyond the master universe, and he calls this a “beachhead on the shores of infinity.” It may not be a mere figure of speech, he says, but a literal event, in the same way that Havona was eternalized together with the appearance of the Infinite Spirit.
w14.123: Sadler suspects that the Cosmos Infinite, in its inner zone, will likewise crystallize all at once, without passing through stages. A portion of the infinity held by the three Absolutes of potentiality would be materialized, mindized, and spiritualized: made experiential.
w14.125: From this comparison Sadler draws the idea of two eternities. With the existential trinitization a cycle of eternity was established [8:1.3]: the first age, without beginning, the age of Havona. The Supreme-Ultimate trinitization may open another cycle, an existential-experiential eternity: the final age, without end, the age of the Cosmos Infinite. The two dawns are remarkably alike. At the first dawn stood the Father and the Son, two existential Deities, together with an existential nuclear base, the Isle of Paradise. At the second dawn stand the Supreme and the Ultimate, two experiential Deities, together with an experiential nuclear base, the completed master universe.
w14.126: 2. A Framework for Thinking about the Cosmos Infinite (orig. pp. 510–511)
w14.127: Thinking about infinity, one easily gets lost in an endless series. Sadler therefore chooses the simplest scheme he can: a conceptual frame of three zones.
w14.128: **The inner zone.** It appears all at once with the trinitization of God the Absolute. It is large enough to dwarf the master universe, perhaps standing to it as the master universe stands to the grand universe. Sadler insists that this is the last reasonable estimate of size anyone can make. It is paired with the activity of the Supreme-Ultimate.
w14.129: **The intermediate zone(s).** These are the successive stages in the development of the Cosmos Infinite. Because they come in sequence, their boundaries cannot be fixed, and they may have no end. They are paired with the activity of the Ultimate-Absolute.
w14.130: **The outer zone(s).** These are conceptual zones that the expanding Cosmos Infinite may never actually reach. They are paired with the function of the last Dual-Deity, the Absolute and the Father-Infinite.
w14.131: Sadler grants that the only relatively certain zone is the inner one, which can appear at once and complete. The outer zones, widening in sequence, may go on without end in eternity.
w14.132: The six Dual-Deity partnerships (106:8.12) and the three zones of the Cosmos Infinite; the pairing of zones and ages is Sadler's conceptual frame
w14.133: 3. Reworking the Levels of Total Deity Function (orig. pp. 511–516)
w14.134: The Foreword of The Urantia Book lists seven levels on which Total Deity functions, running from the static and potential levels through the associative, creative, and evolutional to the supreme and the ultimate [0:1.3–1.10]. The absolute level is missing from that list. Shortly afterward, however, the text speaks of the absolute level on its own.
w14.136: On this basis Sadler holds that there are post-ultimate levels beyond the seven. At one point he considered a ten-level scheme, adding three mirror images of the first three levels, but he set it aside. He recalled how, in Appendix VI, applying experiential measures to Havona had produced nothing but paradoxes, and he concluded that in the post-ultimate ages a new existential-experiential mechanism would be at work. Once the master universe is complete, the creative level ceases, the evolutional level comes to an end once the two experiential Deities have emerged, and the levels of supremacy and ultimacy fall dormant. New levels take their place.
w14.137: Seven levels for the post-ultimate age proposed by Sadler
w14.140: Reservoir of what Deity has willed but not yet actualized
w14.141: First grouping of persons and Deities: the Paradise Trinity
w14.142: Post-ultimate level on which coabsolutes function
w14.143: All existential and experiential Deity reunited in the Trinity of Trinities
w14.144: Absolute potentials become actual directly, without stages of maturation
w14.145: The dynamics of experiential growth pervade the static
w14.146: At the fifth level Sadler contrasts association with reassociation. On the associative level existential Deity became one in the Paradise Trinity. On the reassociative level existential and experiential Deity alike are united again within the Trinity of Trinities. Entry into the sixth level requires two conditions: the growth potential of the finite and the absonite must be entirely exhausted, and experiential Deity and trinity must break through to the absolute level and touch the potential Absolutes directly.
w14.147: The name of the seventh level, static-dynamic, sounds strange, but Sadler points out that the revelation uses this very term in describing the Universal Absolute [0:11.14]. This level can be penetrated but never exhausted. If growth ever consumed every potential, the level would become static once more, but the revelation says this will never happen.
w14.149: Having no end, Sadler adds, does not mean having no beginning or no continuation. The sections on the sixth and seventh levels carry an author's note in the original stating that their concepts were left incomplete.
w14.151: Throughout the master universe Sadler has relied on one principle: Dual-Deity pioneers and trinity consolidates. If that principle holds in the Cosmos Infinite as well, Dual-Deity partnerships will go to work ahead of the Trinity of Trinities. The revelation sets out the whole lineage of these partnerships in a single sentence.
w14.153: Sadler divides these six partnerships into two groups. The first three (Father-Son, Son-Spirit, Spirit-Supreme) begin, develop, and complete the master universe, Havona included. The last three (Supreme-Ultimate, Ultimate-Absolute, and Absolute and Father-Infinite) work beyond the master universe. He then reverses the method of Appendix VI, where he stepped back three times behind the first age, beginning with the Zero Age, and divides the time after the master universe into three ages.
w14.156: The Father and the Son recognizing their oneness and entering eternal partnership [8:0.2]
w14.157: The relation of the Spirit to the Son in later creation [8:3.3]
w14.158: “⟦Q 106:8.12⟧The completion of the cycle of reality⟦/Q⟧” [106:8.12]
w14.159: For the second age Sadler adds a hope. If Personalized Adjusters are destined to minister even on Ultimate-Absolute levels [109:7.5], the finaliters will be there too, since the eternal potential of a finaliter's personal endowment resembles the actuality that a Personalized Adjuster already possesses. As for the relationship God the Absolute will have with the Infinite Father in the third age, Sadler says it can only be guessed at.
w14.161: The table of appendices in the original lists four more appendices that have titles but no text: XXVIII, The Nature of the Deity Absolute; XXIX, The Nature of the Unqualified Absolute; XXX, The Nature of the Universe Absolute; and XXXI, The Concept of the Infinite. Sadler never managed to write them, and so this commentary also ends here. Yet the earlier appendices already point in their direction. God the Absolute grows without end, the Universal Absolute and the Unqualified Absolute can never be exhausted, and everything finally tends toward experiencing the I AM as the Father-Infinite. The unwritten appendices show that Sadler left his study as an open, unfinished question.
w14.162: Sadler expects the trinitization of God the Absolute to bring a “beachhead on the shores of infinity,” the inner zone of the Cosmos Infinite, suddenly into being.
w14.163: The Cosmos Infinite can be pictured as inner, intermediate, and outer zones; only the inner zone is relatively certain.
w14.164: The seven levels of The Urantia Book omit the absolute level. For the post-ultimate age Sadler proposes a new set of seven that includes coabsolute, reassociative, actualizing-potential, and static-dynamic levels.
w14.165: Because statics in growth never appear in the total cosmos, the static-dynamic level is penetrated without end but never exhausted.
w14.166: Of the six partnerships in 106:8.12, the first three work within the master universe and the last three work in the Cosmos Infinite during three post-universe ages.
w14.167: The original contains unfinished sections and four unwritten appendices. Sadler's study ends as an open question.
